content.text: Now attach the handler to the form.

Verifying that `matchesShortcut` correctly handles Shift+Tab by checking the event properties—the key comes through as 'Tab', and all the modifier conditions align properly. Now I'm looking at how the mention menu integrates with this shortcut logic.

There's an accessibility trade-off here: Shift+Tab is the standard way to reverse-tab through focusable elements, so intercepting it in the chat input breaks that convention. But that's exactly what the user requested, and it only activates when there are multiple models available. The real issue is that the handler sits on the form itself, which means Shift+Tab also triggers while focus is on the send or mic buttons—that would break reverse navigation among those toolbar buttons. I should restrict this to fire only when focus is actually inside the prompt editor, keeping the button tab-navigation intact while still supporting the model-cycling behavior the user wants.

Updating the handler to check if the event target is the contenteditable prompt element...
The linter passed without any new issues, so I'm checking the final state of the model select file to make sure everything looks right.

Shift+Tab in the chat input now cycles through the available models.

The shortcut is registered in the existing shortcut system (`lib/keyboard-shortcuts.ts`) alongside the others, so it also appears in the keyboard help dialog under "Chat" and gets platform-correct labels (`⇧Tab` on Mac, `Shift+Tab` elsewhere).

A few deliberate choices about scope, since Shift+Tab normally means "focus the previous element":

- It's handled on the chat input's `<form>`, not globally, so it doesn't hijack reverse tab navigation anywhere else in the app.
- Within the form, it only fires when you're actually typing in the prompt editor. If focus is on the send button or mic button, Shift+Tab still moves focus backward as usual.
- It only fires when there's more than one model configured; otherwise it falls through to normal browser behavior.

I extracted the model list, current selection, and cycling into a `useModelSelection` hook so the chat input and the model dropdown share one source of truth rather than each running their own query and comparison logic. Cycling wraps around to the first model after the last, and if the current selection isn't in the list it starts from the first one.

For discoverability I added a tooltip on the model dropdown trigger reading "Cycle models with ⇧Tab", using the same shortcut definition so the label can't drift out of sync with the actual binding.

I've verified that `useModelSelection` is being called from both components with the same query key, so there's no redundant fetching happening. The type checking for `isTypingInPrompt` using `event.target instanceof HTMLElement` works fine with React's synthetic event system. That covers everything.
